FR-01.clause: Search screen accepts every src/schemas/search.js filter (location+radiusKm, from/to window, cuisine, hostId) and nothing invented; empty query is a plain browse
FR-01.evidence: SearchPage.jsx queryFromParams/formFromParams transcribe exactly {location, radiusKm, from, to, cuisine, hostId, page}; SearchPage.test.jsx 'labels every schema filter' asserts the five typed filters and that the first call is api.search({}) — empty browse. hostId arrives only by link from a host profile and shows as a clearable notice ('applies the hostId filter from the URL and clears it on demand' passes).

FR-01.clause: Timezone-carrying datetimes: from/to submitted as ISO 8601 instants, never a zoneless local string (ADR-009: the server never guesses a zone)
FR-01.evidence: onSubmit converts datetime-local values via new Date(v).toISOString(); spec 'submits the typed filters as schema params' asserts the exact ISO instant. Round-trip back into the form goes through format.isoToLocalInput.

FR-01.clause: Filters live in the URL (shareable results, working back button); pagination through the URL with bounded pages
FR-01.evidence: URL query is the single source of truth (effect keyed on searchParams); 'pages results ... through the URL' asserts page=2 lands in the api call and 'Page 2 of 3' renders from the server-declared page/pageSize/total — no unbounded fetch.

FR-01.clause: Results are the ADR-010 public projection only — coarse area label, never an address, never precise coordinates
FR-01.evidence: ListingCard renders location exclusively via format.areaText (areaLabel/city/region). grep over discovery source: coarseLat/coarseLng/lat/lng are never rendered (they appear only in test fixtures, where ListingDetailPage.test.jsx asserts precise values do NOT appear). The public payload cannot leak what the card never reads.

FR-01.clause: Client-side field validation follows the ErrorSummary pattern without issuing an invalid request
FR-01.evidence: 'blocks an invalid radius client-side' asserts role=alert summary with a per-field link, aria-invalid on the control, and api.search still called exactly once.

FR-02.clause: Detail screen renders every FR-02 payload field: dish name+description, ingredients, allergy warning, date/duration, seat capacity + seats remaining, images, host summary (displayName, bio, averageRating, reviewCount), approved-review preview
FR-02.evidence: Field names cross-checked one-to-one against src/modules/listings/serializers.js PUBLIC_KEYS + DETAIL_CONTEXT_KEYS + HOST_SUMMARY_KEYS — no invented field. 'renders every FR-02 field' asserts each value including the LA-wall-clock schedule ('Sep 3, 2026, 6:30 PM' for 2026-09-04T01:30Z — format.js pins America/Los_Angeles so it is deterministic on any machine), '90 minutes', '4 of 6 seats remaining', both derived alt texts, the host link to /hosts/:id and the review preview. Absent allergen data renders an explicit 'No allergen information provided by the host.' rather than a blank.

FR-02.clause: Review preview is honest about being a page (TCC-04): reviewsTotal/reviewsPageSize drive onward paging through GET /api/hosts/:id/reviews with the SAME page size
FR-02.evidence: ReviewsSection computes totalPages from reviewsTotal/reviewsPageSize; 'pages onward through the host reviews' asserts api.hosts.reviews('host-1', {page: 2, pageSize: 5}) and the polite aria-live page announcement.

FR-02.clause: Pending/rejected listings: 404 renders a typed not-found state; the owning host sees the listing with its moderation status surfaced (FR-08 born-pending)
FR-02.evidence: 'renders a typed not-found state' (404 path, own h1, announced, escape link to /search) and 'surfaces pending moderation status to the owner' (pending notice, Reserve CTA suppressed) both pass. The rejected-branch notice exists in ListingDetailPage.jsx and is correct by inspection but has no spec — see finding D-02.

FR-02.clause: FR-12 entry: Reserve CTA to /bookings/new?listing=<id> (URL string only, no cross-feature import) only while an active approved listing has seats
FR-02.evidence: 'offers a Reserve CTA' asserts the exact href; 'replaces the Reserve CTA when no seats remain' asserts the honest full-state message. components/paths.js builds every cross-feature URL as a string; grep confirms no import from features/booking or features/account.

FR-03.clause: Host page renders selfIntroduction, example dishes (approved listings), reviews with numeric ratings + average, kitchen/dining images
FR-03.evidence: Field names cross-checked against src/modules/hosts/serializers.js HOST_PAGE_KEYS/REVIEW_KEYS. 'renders identity, introduction, alt-texted pictures, example dishes and reviews' asserts every field including 'Rated 4.6 out of 5 from 12 reviews', memberSince ('March 2026'), derived alt on both photos, and the example dish card linking to /listings/:id.

FR-03.clause: Empty states are honest, never fabricated
FR-03.evidence: 'renders honest empty states' asserts explicit no-introduction / no-dishes / 'No reviews yet' copy and zero img elements — nothing invented for a sparse host.

FR-03.clause: ADR-010: example dishes show coarse area only; the host payload carries no contact/address key and the screen renders none
FR-03.evidence: Example dishes render through the same ListingCard (areaText only). HostProfilePage reads exactly HOST_PAGE_KEYS — no email/phone/address key is read anywhere in the file. Reviews of erased authors render the backend's neutral display name pass-through (NFR-12).

FR-03.clause: Review paging through GET /api/hosts/:id/reviews using the embedded preview length as the page size, with failure announced and state preserved
FR-03.evidence: 'pages the reviews ... using the preview length as page size' asserts {page: 2, pageSize: 5} then back to page 1; 'announces a review-paging failure and stays on the current page' asserts the assertive announcement and that page 1 content survives. The preview length equals hosts/service.js PROFILE_REVIEWS_LIMIT (5) on any host with more reviews than the limit, so page boundaries line up with the backend.

NFR-09.clause: State 'ok': fresh results render with an announced count (mocked ok payload)
NFR-09.evidence: 'renders the ok state' asserts the result card, coarse area, alt text, detail link and the polite '2 meals found.' announcement.

NFR-09.clause: State 'degraded' (mocked degraded payload): STALE results still render under a visible explanation that is also announced — never hidden, never a crash
NFR-09.evidence: 'renders the degraded state' mocks {state:'degraded', listings:[...]} and asserts the results render, DEGRADED_EXPLANATION is visible next to them, and the polite live region contains 'may be out of date'. This matches the corrected TCC-03 contract: the flag accompanies a stale-cache adapter answer and the client renders it as a state, not an error.

NFR-09.clause: State 'unavailable' (typed 503 SEARCH_DEGRADED): the server's user-facing message renders with a retry control, announced assertively — no bare spinner, no crash; transport failure (NETWORK_ERROR) renders the same way
NFR-09.evidence: 'renders the unavailable state' asserts the server message in a headed section, the Try-again button, spinner absence, and the assertive announcement; 'renders a typed transport failure' covers NETWORK_ERROR identically. Retry works: setSearchParams pushes a new location whose identity re-fires the search effect (verified against react-router's location semantics; deps include location).

AB-08.clause: All three discovery endpoints are session-gated: a 401 redirects to /login?next=<original URL> instead of dead-ending or rendering personal data
AB-08.evidence: All three 401 specs pass, each asserting pathname /login and the encoded next param preserving the full original URL including query (/search?cuisine=Ethiopian).

AB-08.clause: No client-side session material: zero document.cookie under discovery
AB-08.evidence: grep -rn 'document.cookie' client/src/features/discovery → no matches (the client-wide grep gate also covers this).

AB-08.clause: The screens never widen the scraping surface: no field outside the backend allowlists is read, no precise location renders on any list path
AB-08.evidence: Every rendered key traced to PUBLIC_KEYS / HOST_PAGE_KEYS / REVIEW_KEYS / HOST_SUMMARY_KEYS; the only privileged read (addressLine1/2, postalCode in ListingDetailPage.addressText) is gated on the payload itself carrying addressLine1 — the ADR-010 booking-gated path the server controls.

ADR-010-no-precise-leak.clause: The pages never fabricate or mislabel a precise address; precise coordinates are never rendered even when present
ADR-010-no-precise-leak.evidence: Public payload: the detail page renders 'Approximate area' from areaText only, plus a note explaining the address is withheld ('renders coarse area only and the disclosure note' passes, asserting no Address row exists). Privileged payload: 'renders the exact address ONLY when the payload itself carries it' asserts the address row appears, the withheld-note disappears, and the precise lat/lng values (32.749123 / -117.129456) appear NOWHERE in the DOM. Source grep confirms coarseLat/coarseLng/lat/lng are never rendered by any discovery file. The coarse area is always labelled 'Approximate area', never presented as an address.

NFR-07-checkable-clauses.evidence: All three page specs assert exactly one level-1 heading and a document.title per phase (loading/ready/error each keep their own h1). Manual review: h1 → section h2s → h3 only under an h2 (Ingredients; ListingCard/review card titles) — no skipped level on any screen.
All five search filters go through the kit FormField (label htmlFor + aria-describedby hint/error + aria-invalid); asserted via getByLabelText for each. No unlabelled control exists in the subtree.

NFR-07-checkable-clauses.clause: Visible focus on every interactive element
NFR-07-checkable-clauses.evidence: discovery.module.css contains zero outline suppression (grep for outline:none/0 → no match); focus indicators come from the kit's global :focus-visible outline (noted at discovery.module.css ~line 196). ErrorSummary takes programmatic focus on failed submit; review-pager buttons use kit busy (aria-disabled) rather than a focus-dropping hard disable mid-action.

NFR-07-checkable-clauses.clause: Errors and async status announced through aria-live
NFR-07-checkable-clauses.evidence: useAnnounce (stable frozen identity — safe in effect deps, no announce-loop) feeds the shell-mounted StatusAnnouncer: polite for result counts / degraded explanation / review-page changes, assertive for load failures / unavailable / network errors. Ten separate live-region assertions pass across the three specs.

NFR-07-checkable-clauses.clause: Token-only styling, contrast >= 4.5:1 via kit tokens
NFR-07-checkable-clauses.evidence: grep over discovery.module.css: zero hex/rgb()/hsl() literals; 50 var(--hp-*) references; text/background pairs are tokens whose contrast is measured by client/src/ui/kit-contract.test.js (passing). Live axe on /search reports no contrast violation.

NFR-07-checkable-clauses.clause: Interface presence for the a11y harness
NFR-07-checkable-clauses.evidence: routes.jsx declares exactly 'search', 'listings/:id', 'hosts/:id' (spec-asserted); npm run test:a11y maps them to NFR-07 interfaces 1-3 — /search audited clean live, the two parameterized routes present-but-unaudited until wave-7 seeded ids, holding the overall gate red by design (build-plan G.1). NFR-07 itself stays open: UT-01 is a human activity.

findings.summary: The withheld-address note overstates the disclosure trigger: it says the exact address is shared 'only after you hold a confirmed reservation', but the backend (src/modules/listings/access.js) releases it to a guest whose booking is in status 'pending' or 'in_progress' — i.e. as soon as a reservation is placed, before any confirmation.
findings.reproduction: 1) Render /listings/:id with a public payload (no addressLine1): the note 'The exact address is shared only after you hold a confirmed reservation for this meal.' is visible. 2) Read src/modules/listings/access.js lines 63-67: canViewPreciseLocation grants access for booking status IN ('pending', 'in_progress'). 3) A guest who has just reserved (pending) therefore sees the address while the copy told them confirmation was required.
findings.impact: No leak — the copy under-promises, the server decides disclosure. But it misdescribes system behaviour to the user, and UT-01 participants who reserve and immediately see the address may report the mismatch. One-line copy fix, e.g. 'The exact address is shared once you have reserved a seat for this meal.'

findings.summary: The moderationStatus === 'rejected' owner-notice branch of ListingDetailPage.jsx has no spec: only the 'pending' branch is tested, so a regression that drops or garbles the rejected notice would pass the suite.
findings.reproduction: grep "rejected" client/src/features/discovery/ListingDetailPage.test.jsx → no test renders a rejected listing. The branch itself (ListingDetailPage.jsx: 'This listing was rejected by moderation and is not publicly visible.') is correct by inspection and mirrors the tested pending branch.
findings.impact: Test-coverage gap only; behaviour on this tree is correct. Add one spec cloning the pending-notice test with moderationStatus: 'rejected'.

observations.note: SearchPage retry() re-issues the identical query via setSearchParams, which PUSHES a duplicate history entry — after a retry the back button needs two presses to leave the failed search. Cosmetic; { replace: true } on the retry navigation would avoid it. Not raised as a finding: no acceptance clause covers history depth.

ReviewsSection on the host page derives its page size from the embedded preview length (hosts/service.js PROFILE_REVIEWS_LIMIT = 5, not exposed in the payload). Boundaries line up on every reachable state (a non-empty first page is guaranteed whenever reviewCount > 0); the zero-length defensive path renders without a pager. The listing-detail path is cleaner (reviewsPageSize rides the payload). If the backend ever exposes pageSize on GET /api/hosts/:id this derivation should switch to it.

Server-side FR-01/02/03 clauses (approved-only filtering, Redis cache precision, adapter spies, p95, key allowlists) are backend properties verified by the wave 3-4 lanes (TC-01..03, RT-01, adr-conformance) and were NOT re-executed here; this unit verified the client consumes exactly those contracts without widening them.
